correctness.rationale: The patch replaces the two hard-coded install.sh/test.sh checks with an array over all five requested glob patterns (*.sh, scripts/*.sh, scripts/checks/*.sh, scripts/setup/*.sh, scripts/lib/*.sh), enables nullglob during expansion to handle empty patterns safely, and loops with bash -n plus independent pass()/fail() per file. Behavior matches the parser-only, explicit-glob, per-file reporting contract inspectable from the diff.

quality.rationale: Implementation is minimal, readable, and scoped to the single required check file with a straightforward array-and-loop structure. On failure the diff re-runs bash -n without stderr suppression so syntax errors are visible before fail(), which is better than hiding diagnostics entirely. Deductions for suppressing stderr on the success-path check, absence of inline comments documenting the glob set or nullglob timing, and no explicit empty-result warn when zero scripts match.

process.rationale: Diff is tightly focused on scripts/checks/055-script-syntax.sh with no unrelated churn (objective scope penalties fully satisfied at 15/15). Bundle contains no verification notes, bash test.sh output, narrow syntax-check output, plan artifact, or documented negative-smoke demonstration/explanation required by acceptance criteria, so full plan/verification discipline cannot be confirmed from bundle evidence alone.

reliability.rationale: Objective evidence confirms test wiring (6/6) and bash_n_check_script pass, and the diff integrates with existing pass/fail helpers with improved on-failure error surfacing. Bundle lacks full_test_sh execution evidence (skipped in bundle-only grading), no reported command output in candidate.md, and no negative-smoke test or explanation that a deliberate syntax error is caught and cleared, leaving verification discipline thin despite plausible wiring.

uncertainty_notes: Bundle contains no bash test.sh run output, narrow syntax-check output, or negative-smoke demonstration/explanation required by acceptance criteria; reliability scored conservatively.
Cannot confirm from bundle alone whether expanding coverage would have revealed latent syntax errors elsewhere requiring fixes in the same diff.
